items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Well, you’re in the archive, in the collections, with Abbey Lincoln, Quincy Jones, Jimmy Heath, with Shirley Horn, with Ella Fitzgerald...

ctx.x: I think that I was completely fine with all this, and I’ve been very busy. I haven’t had a chance to really absorb it, until your director just said what he said about sharing a category with... Say it again.
Well, you’re in the archive, in the collections, with Abbey Lincoln, Quincy Jones, Jimmy Heath, with Shirley Horn, with Ella Fitzgerald...

Had you said this in the beginning of our interview, I would have been speechless. I wouldn’t have been able to think of anything to say. Actually, I didn’t know a whole lot about it, because I haven’t had much time to attend many of these. I went when some of my favorite legends were inducted. I really see this as an award for a We thing rather than a Me thing. There are many people, as I’ve mentioned in this interview, who did this with me, who made all this possible. So for me, it’s a win for the Jazz…
